title: Count The Number of Winning Sequences
summary: Alice and Bob participate in a fantasy battle game consisting of n rounds.
statement: Alice and Bob participate in a fantasy battle game consisting of n rounds. In each round, Alice summons one of three magical creatures: a Fire Dragon ('F'), a Water Serpent ('W'), or an Earth Golem ('E'). Bob's sequence of summons is unknown but must avoid summoning the same creature in consecutive rounds. Points are awarded based on the following rules: - If Alice summons a Fire Dragon and Bob summons an Earth Golem, Bob scores a point. - If Alice summons a Water Serpent and Bob summons a Fire Dragon, Bob scores a point. - If Alice summons an Earth Golem and Bob summons a Water Serpent, Bob scores a point. - If both summon the same creature, no points are awarded. Alice's sequence of creatures is given as a string s, where each character represents her choice in each round: - 'F' means Alice summons a Fire Dragon. - 'W' means Alice summons a Water Serpent. - 'E' means Alice summons an Earth Golem. Bob wins if he scores more points than Alice at the end of n rounds. Calculate the number of distinct sequences Bob can use to ensure his score is strictly greater than Alice's, and return this number modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s contains 1–1,000 moves from F, W, E.
Bob chooses F/W/E without repeating his previous move; W beats F, E beats W, and F beats E.
Count Bob sequences with a strictly positive final score difference modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Only the previous Bob move and current score difference affect future choices.
Map each round to score change -1,0,+1 and aggregate counts by (last move,difference).
Try the two allowed next moves from every state, then sum positive-difference states.
The state retains every constraint-relevant fact and merges only equivalent prefixes, so all legal sequences are counted once.
editorial: The state retains every constraint-relevant fact and merges only equivalent prefixes, so all legal sequences are counted once.

tests.explanation: Exactly WFW, FWF, and WEW beat Alice while avoiding repeated moves.
There are eighteen legal Bob sequences with a positive final score.
